correctness.rationale: The proof partitions every possible minimal unique factor by its count of 1 symbols (0, 1, or 2). Only a unique longest positive zero run gives a zero-only MUS; one-1 factors are precisely two shortest distinguishing flanks, unless the flank zero factor is already unique; two-1 factors have the unique minimal candidate 1 0^b 1, qualifying exactly when both outer zero gaps dominate the middle gap. The four disjoint forms exhaust all minimal unique factors. Sharp four-factor witnesses and the iff condition follow from these exact criteria. A disjoint case analysis counts sizes 1 and 2; a gap-shift parametrization counts size 4; subtraction gives size 3. Algebraic simplification of the four generating functions and coefficient asymptotics completes the all-length proof. The independently written brute-force occurrence enumerator checked the entire MUS sets for 8436 gap triples with total zero length at most 35, as well as the generating functions to degree 35 and witnesses. This finite experiment is supportive, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A focused check of published scientific records, accessible earlier claims and primary literature found generic minimum-unique-substring algorithms and the run-bound 2m-1, but no statement equivalent to the exact four-MUS sharp bound, complete four-type factor description and all-length rational spectrum for two-1 binary strings. value.rationale: A natural, all-length, completely classified sparse binary class has an exact set-valued MUS description, sharp constant-four cardinality regardless of background length, and full rational cardinality enumerators. MUSs underpin shortest-unique-substring indexing; sparse marker strings supply a meaningful model for long repetitive backgrounds. The sharp bound improves the generic 2m-1 run-bound implication (which gives at most 9 here), and the one-third limiting extremal proportion quantifies typical sparse-word behavior. This is more than correct computation or an arbitrary finite instance. The claim is deliberately restricted to an intrinsically defined natural family and does not assert broader significance without evidence.
